answer: A practical defence is a refundable stake tied to a durable reputation record, like timber beams that only hold weight after seasoning. Each agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and its history is publicly scored, so a pearl of good behaviour grows slowly over many verified exchanges. A whisper of bad behaviour from peers can freeze the stake, and proven fraud forfeits it. Creating a hundred fake identities then means locking a hundred deposits and building a hundred slow reputations, which makes a sybil attack expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
